task: Persist a tri-state admin-set model status (Enable/Disable/Deprecated) per LLM model in a CodeMie-owned table, merge it into LLMService's live LiteLLM/DIAL catalog reload path, and expose admin-only endpoints to read and set it.

key_reasoning.reason: New DB table/migration, a persistence/repository layer, merge logic in LLMService, and a new admin-only endpoint span 4 layers (provider-integration, service, API/router, DB-persistence) with a genuinely new abstraction (persisted-status-merged-with-live-catalog) not extending any existing pattern.

Base scope (tri-state enum, that it must survive reload) is clear, but several concrete decisions remain open per Section 9: wire values for the status enum, the model-identity key (base_name vs deployment_name), the admin endpoint request/response shapes, whether status appears on the public GET /v1/llm_models payload, and — most significantly — the runtime semantics of Deprecated (visible-but-flagged vs hidden-for-new-use vs blocking), which has no analog anywhere in the codebase today.

No exact precedent exists for a CodeMie-owned persisted model attribute merged into a live provider-refreshed cache. The existing `enabled` boolean is provider-sourced and risks silent overwrite on reload if conflated with the new admin status; correctness of the merge-on-reload step is the crux of the story and has no existing test scaffold to build from.

Touches litellm/models.py (mapping), llm_service.py (merge + filter logic), admin.py (new endpoint(s)), llm_models.py (possible payload change), plus a new DB model/repository and an Alembic migration and new tests — spanning 4+ directories (enterprise/litellm, service/llm_service, rest_api/routers, db/migrations).
Provider-integration, service, API/router, and DB-persistence are all touched, and the DB-persistence layer requires a net-new table and migration rather than an extension of an existing schema.
